claims.text: Heating the alloy at approximately 650°C for 2 hours followed by controlled cooling will form finely dispersed coherent precipitates.
The proposed 650°C treatment and controlled cooling will transform straight grain boundaries into serrated grain boundaries.
The treatment will improve mechanical durability relative to the untreated state.
The treatment will improve room-temperature creep resistance relative to the untreated state.
The treatment will improve corrosion resistance relative to the untreated state.
The as-fabricated alloy has a relatively coarse precipitate distribution.
Straight grain boundaries produce suboptimal tensile and creep properties.
Straight grain boundaries produce suboptimal corrosion properties.
Controlled slow cooling promotes precipitate refinement.
Coherent precipitates pin grain boundaries and promote grain-boundary serration.
Precipitate obstacles restrict dislocation motion and grain-boundary migration.
Serrated grain boundaries distribute strain more evenly, reduce local strain concentration, and resist intergranular cracking.
Additional grain-boundary nucleation sites facilitate thicker and less defective passivation films.
Thicker and less defective passivation films improve corrosion resistance.
The treated alloy will have greater tensile fracture strain than the untreated or air-cooled baseline.
The treated alloy will have longer creep rupture life at approximately 650°C than the untreated or air-cooled baseline.
The treated alloy will exhibit lower corrosion current density and higher pitting potential than the baseline.
A sufficiently controlled cooling rate is required to obtain the desired precipitate and grain-boundary structure.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis claims improved room-temperature creep resistance, whereas the conditions and falsification experiment evaluate creep at approximately 650°C.

The initial state is described as having coarse precipitates and the intervention as promoting precipitate refinement, but the cited slow-cooling evidence reports coarsening of γ′ particles as the route to grain-boundary serration.
